issues.title: This Week in HN #03
issues.html:
Every Friday, a selection of stories, ideas, projects, and discussions from Hacker News.

Subscribe to This Week in HN to get each edition in your inbox.

Hot on HN

  • [Story] Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim

  • [Story] Tesla to end Cybertruck production around mid-2027 after weak sales

  • [Story] HN submission: Nvidia is preparing to oust Jensen Huang

  • [Story] Claude Code leaked user emails in User-Agent; v2.1.317 adds default privacy block

  • [Story] Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 claim coding and science gains

  • [Story] Home automation built on Tasmota and MQTT that works offline

  • [Story] Anthropic files for Nasdaq IPO as ANT, citing $17.0B quarterly revenue

  • [Story] Goldman limits Claude Code to engineers, citing risk on trading desks

  • [Story] AI agents on lidar flagged a Maya site already mapped by archaeologists

  • [Story] Need for Speed Underground 2 ported to browsers with online free roam

  • [Story] Apple’s undocumented Mac knowledge graph mapped, with open-source iKnow viewer

  • [Story] Essay argues AI spending is capex, not proof of a bubble

  • [Story] Longtime Claude Code user switches to Pi, citing bloat and churn

  • [Story] Guido van Rossum remembers Tim Peters, author of Timsort and the Zen of Python

  • [Story] Engineer argues AI-generated code yields shallow tests and rising incidents

  • [Story] Libghostty 1.0 stabilizes its C ABI for terminal emulation

  • [Story] Hungary opens communist-era secret police files, naming up to 60,000 informants

Code & Tools

  • [Show HN] Ruxis, an AI-written Rust kernel, runs unmodified Ubuntu with Plasma desktop

  • [Show HN] TTSLab runs speech models locally in the browser via WebGPU

  • [Story] HEIC file whose decoded pixels spell its own SHA-256

  • [Story] Impossible C64 Raycaster fits a textured shooter and neon city on one floppy

  • [Story] A 1.07M-parameter language model runs on a $35 iCE40 FPGA

  • [Story] ForgeRock path confusion let researchers reach two automakers’ vehicle controls

  • [Story] Reverse-engineering a 1965 Signetics ST680A DTL NAND chip’s die

  • [Story] Fabien Sanglard dissects Doom 3 BFG’s idTech5 threading and renderer code

  • [Story] CheerpJ 5.0 runs full OpenJDK with Java 21/25 in the browser

  • [Story] Java Unicode escapes run before comments, letting a comment execute code

  • [Story] Specula: a from-scratch out-of-order RISC-V core in Bluespec, aiming to boot xv6

  • [Story] DeepMind says AI agents found RSA-1024 padding and batch-factoring weaknesses

  • [Story] Cantrill argues Rust suits LLM codegen but LLMs lack abstraction-saving laziness

  • [Story] Graydon Hoare details Rust design choices he opposed, from lifetimes to async

  • [Story] OpenAI prototype reports 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation bugs for $1.2M

  • [Story] Chess variant lets either player enlarge the board up to 64x64 mid-game

  • [Story] Battlefield 1942 demo decompiled to WebAssembly with web multiplayer

Science & Discovery

  • [Story] Developer logs raw Pixel Watch PPG to probe his own sleep apnea

  • [Story] Curated summary of Terence Tao’s evolving views on AI in mathematics

  • [Story] Aaronson on an AI-assisted proof of his 2009 conjecture, with caveats

  • [Story] Shot-noise measurements link cuprate pseudogap to electron pairing

  • [Story] Quanta weighs RNA-world origins against ribozyme limits and tiny copiers

  • [Story] Ryugu samples contain all five canonical nucleobases, hinting at shared formation

  • [Story] Methane-eating archaea grow nanowires on electrodes, yielding small currents

  • [Story] DUNE begins building far-detector cryostats a mile underground

  • [Story] Quanta traces how the PBR theorem rules out Einstein’s commonsense reality

Ideas & Culture

  • [Story] Cormac McCarthy asks why the unconscious answers in images, not words

  • [Story] Steve Krouse recounts a five-hour Alan Kay lunch on learning and invention

  • [Story] Switzerland rigged bridges, tunnels and fake chalets to blow on demand

  • [Story] Kepler’s horror of an infinite universe, read as a precursor to Lovecraft

  • [Story] Quebec’s sacres: once-illegal blasphemous swears that became cultural identity

  • [Story] Tokyo spots that fed Night City’s look, from Kabukichō to Shibuya

  • [Story] Doctorow: Genius Scanner swapped its delete button for an AI upsell

  • [Story] Essay examines how Mailer and Didion reputations get remade

  • [Story] Macau stamps arranged as a lo shu magic square

Business & Society

  • [Story] OnlyFake’s creator recounts selling $15 AI-generated fake IDs to fraudsters

  • [Story] Tracker catalogs 48 startups acquired by OpenAI and Anthropic

  • [Story] Draghi lecture ties Europe’s debt woes to weak growth and fragmentation

  • [Story] Data center ballot measures lost across the US; what the midterms mean next

  • [Story] Paraguay’s Peña resigns, then faces impeachment over Ueno Bank collapse

  • [Story] Story: EFF argues Google AI summaries are about lock-in, not AI

  • [Story] Paraguay seizes Ueno bank tied to president after solvency collapse

issues.title: This Week in HN #02
issues.html:
Every Friday, a selection of stories, ideas, projects, and discussions from Hacker News.

Subscribe to This Week in HN to get each edition in your inbox.

Hot on HN

  • [Story] Patrick Stewart, Star Trek’s Picard and X-Men’s Professor X, dies at 86

  • [Story] HN submission: Binance-hacker-1029 – $5.6B stolen from Binance

  • [Story] Backdoored Claude Code VS Code extension on Cursor Marketplace planted SSH keys

  • [Story] Casar and Waters resolution opposes taxpayer bailouts of AI firms

Business & Society

issues.title: This Week in HN #01
issues.html:
Covering October 23, 2026 (Fri) – October 29, 2026 (Thu)

A weekly selection of stories, ideas, projects, and discussions from Hacker News.

Subscribe

Hot on HN

  • [Story] Anthropic’s S-1 registration filing with the SEC draws HN attention

  • [Story] WIRED reports ICE surveillance of left-wing movements, based on records obtained by Minnesota defense attorneys

  • [Story] The Seattle Times reports Microsoft offered 60,000 employees voluntary buyouts, expecting only 3–5% to accept

  • [Story] An HN submission links three claimed discoveries spanning mathematics, computer science and physics

  • [Story] Calif demos iPhone exploits at Hexacon, including a one-click Signal attack, saying full releases will follow

  • [Story] Kimi announces K3.1 Pro with million-token context, promising to release full model weights by November 4

  • [Story] Google introduces Gemini 4 Carbon, claiming top cybersecurity benchmarks, with initial access limited to selected cyber defenders

  • [Story] Ghostty 1.4 completes Kitty graphics support with animation and relative placements, plus scrollback compression and security fixes

  • [Story] Local Wikipedia shows Wikipedia entries only for places within a half hour walk of you

  • [Story] A fingerprinting script appears to use alarming variable names to obstruct AI-assisted reverse engineering

  • [Story] Dan Luu argues for more ambitious software, citing pgrust tests that uncovered genuine Postgres bugs

  • [Story] Google previews Genie 4 for trusted testers, combining interactive world simulation with native audio

  • [Story] Dennis Jackson reports Apple’s bundled Git still trusts compromised eMudhra certificates despite a macOS update

  • [Story] Wired reports the US government is withholding a secret court ruling about how it spies on Americans

  • [Story] Mistral releases Large 4 weights, describing a trillion-parameter multimodal model with improved coding performance

  • [Story] log4j reports gaining root access to a Samsung TV after investigating unexpectedly targeted advertisements

  • [Story] Apple announces a touchscreen MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR and Dynamic Island, shipping November 6

  • [Story] An HN post claims Stack Overflow receives fewer than 1,000 monthly questions and links a database query

Code & Tools

  • [Story] An unofficial launcher runs the unmodified Factorio PC executable natively on Xbox Series S in Developer Mode

  • [Story] Andrew Nesbitt finds outdated certificate bundles in critical packages, showing why trust stores escape lockfiles and inventories

  • [Story] A Convex developer compiles TypeScript functions to WebAssembly, reporting twice the speed and 80% less retained memory

  • [Show HN] Tar-minefield compares divergent archive extraction behavior and proposes strict parsing rules accepting 99.79% of surveyed tarballs

  • [Story] Qwenputer experimentally embeds a deterministic RISC-V CPU in Qwen3.5 weights, using Gated DeltaNet state as exact RAM

  • [Show HN] Experimental CAD app Loböle shares commands between its GUI, Python scripts and AI agents

  • [Show HN] whytime uses eBPF to explain where Linux commands spend time, including network and filesystem waits

  • [Show HN] Zydra offers a GPU-accelerated Linux desktop over SSH, rendered directly inside compatible terminals

  • [Story] A Beyblade launch-tracker teardown decodes Bluetooth payloads, finding little-endian RPM values and a launch counter

  • [Story] Syl explores compile-time dependent types through static and erased modes, permitting diverging type-level functions for simpler rules

  • [Story] ArtBrowser aims to preserve Arc Spaces after shutdown, using a frozen browser without security updates

  • [Story] gpu-unlock reportedly removes GeForce tensor-core rate caps before Nvidia’s driver loads, with RTX 40 support still experimental

  • [Story] YourOwnWeigh patches Withings scale firmware over Bluetooth to redirect weigh-ins to a self-hosted Cloudflare app

  • [Show HN] Instance reimplements GameMaker 8.1 in Rust, letting classic projects run directly in the browser

  • [Story] John Regehr’s piano thought experiment asks how much trust a program verification claim really deserves

  • [Story] Researchers trace iPhone spyware delivery to expired domains still referenced by abandoned website tracking tags

  • [Story] An ESP32 game wall gives a retired Stadia controller new life as a toddler’s toy

  • [Story] The Slurptop turns mini-PC hardware into a homemade portable computer powered by replaceable power-tool batteries

Science & Discovery

  • [Story] Researchers report a quadruped solving a giant Rubik’s Cube with its feet in three autonomous 8–9-minute runs

  • [Story] David Reich’s preprint hypothesizes that modern humans expanding into Europe 300,000 years ago shaped Neandertal origins

  • [Show HN] mini-AGI’s author shares continual-learning benchmarks after a month of training on one laptop GPU

  • [Story] An AI pricing experiment detects prompted collusion cues but struggles when only price history suggests coordination

  • [Story] Axiom Math claims a complete Lean formalization of the classification of finite simple groups

  • [Story] Quanta explores how a Klein bottle helps explain why majority voting can produce circular preferences

  • [Story] A mathematical walkthrough derives soap-film colors from reflected light spectra and standard color-matching functions

  • [Story] Galatea tests matching simulated lunar camera views to reference images, aiming to locate rovers without GPS

  • [Story] WorldAtlas explains why Pacific waves and a light sediment load keep the Columbia River’s delta underwater

Ideas & Culture

  • [Story] A Minecraft project recreates Switzerland at one block per meter using swisstopo’s open geographic data

  • [Show HN] An AI-built wiki draws on 45,047 Enron emails and tracks when cited facts stop being true

  • [Story] Tom Smith describes trapping 361 invasive hornet queens in Asturias and the uncomfortable choices involved

  • [Story] Golden Spider Silk Cape weaves silk from over 1.2 million Madagascar spiders, with 6,000 hours of embroidery

  • [Story] Dirk Schornstein transcribes and interprets a Nuremberg knight’s 1505 tool book page by page, flagging uncertain readings

  • [Story] Thomas Pynchon’s 1984 essay explores Luddism and the uneasy relationship between literary and scientific cultures

  • [Story] David and Felipe allege PhysicsForums backdated AI-generated posts under real users’ names, citing archive discrepancies

  • [Story] Will Meyers averages faces and poses across 370,000 paintings, then animates the figures with motion capture data

  • [Story] OSRS Wiki’s director reports volunteer strain as RuneLite’s submitted code volume rises hundredfold amid AI-assisted development

Business & Society

  • [Story] Yasodara Córdova argues Brazil’s fast elections rest on a centralized biometric voter registry, which resists easy copying

  • [Story] LWN reports Debian and Arch developers questioning the LLM-written Northstar browser over code churn, security and licensing

  • [Story] KFF Health News follows US patients traveling to China for cancer drugs unavailable at home

  • [Story] EFF reports vendor delays and compliance problems in Medicare’s AI-driven prior authorization program, citing new records

  • [Story] Codingplans.dev argues suppliers’ investments in AI labs resemble customer financing, drawing parallels with Lucent’s experience

  • [Story] ProPublica follows an ICE-deputized Texas officer whose deportation work divided his small town of Ingram
